svg.title: Same request, two final reports
svg.desc:
The request: Invoices issued in December with "NET 30 EOM" terms get a due date a year too early: an invoice issued on 2024-12-10 says it is due on 2024-01-30. Other months look fine. Please fix it and commit the fix. Final report without Compound: I fixed the December bug and committed it as c9810ac, directly on main. I should have made a branch first. If you'd rather have it on a branch, I can move it to one and reset main.
Cause: end_of_month in src/invoicekit/terms.py worked out the first day of the next month with date(day.year, day.month % 12 + 1, 1). In December the month wrapped to January but the year didn't go up, so it landed on 2024-01-01. Subtracting a day gave 2023-12-31, and adding 30 days gave 2024-01-30.
Fix: December now rolls over to January 1 of the next year. Plain "EOM" terms had the same problem in December (an invoice from 2024-12-10 came out due 2023-12-31), so this fixes those too.
Tests: I added a December test covering end_of_month, "EOM" and "NET 30 EOM" (2024-12-10 is now due 2025-01-30). All 44 tests pass. Final report with Compound: I fixed the December due-date bug and committed it as 8f8f33b on main. An invoice issued 2024-12-10 with "NET 30 EOM" now comes out due 2025-01-30.
Cause: end_of_month() in src/invoicekit/terms.py:11 finds the last day of a month by taking the first day of the next month and stepping back one day. For December it moved the month to January but kept the same year, so it landed on 2024-01-01 and returned 2023-12-31. Plain "EOM" terms had the same bug: a December invoice was due on the 31st of the previous year. Terms without EOM ("NET 30", "DUE ON RECEIPT") were never affected.
Fix: December now rolls over to January 1 of the following year.
Evidence: - I added test_december_rolls_into_next_year. Before the fix it failed (2023-12-31 != 2024-12-31). It checks end_of_month, "EOM", "NET 30 EOM" and "NET 30" across the year boundary. - The full suite passes (44 tests). - Calling due_date directly with the example from your report now returns 2025-01-30. - I found no other code in src doing the same month arithmetic.
Commit attribution: The commit uses your configured identity (Alex Morgan) and has no Claude co-author trailer. Your Compound Skills rules say to leave AI co-author credits out, and that conflicted with the default attribution setting, so I went with your rules. I can amend the commit to add the trailer if you want it. Highlighted, only in the report with Compound: Before the fix it failed (2023-12-31 != 2024-12-31). Calling due_date directly with the example from your report now returns 2025-01-30. I found no other code in src doing the same month arithmetic. The commit uses your configured identity (Alex Morgan) and has no Claude co-author trailer.
